Three independent defences: separate tables, no generic write path on MarkRepo, and a SQLite authorizer installed on every connection that refuses INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on founder-owned tables outside founder_write_allowed(). Migration 004 adds founder_write_attempt, auditing both refusals and sanctioned writes. Acceptance proven: the attempt raises, the exception names the table, an audit row is written, and it is logged at ERROR. Found and fixed a real hole: SQLite runs the authorizer at PREPARE time and Python caches prepared statements, so the second identical write skipped the guard entirely — cached_statements=0 is load-bearing. guard.py 100% branch coverage, 152/152 mutations caught.
